card.name: Mid-sentence points in warning statements
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a connecting word at a clause boundary inside boxed-warning or pregnancy-warning sentences. Also fires on a few words inside risk phrases such as fetal renal dysfunction or prophylaxis.

modes.label: Clause break after a instruction
modes.description: A period or semicolon ending a clause about treatment or screening, just before a follow-up sentence.
modes.example: administer an opioid antagonist<<.>> Because the duration of opioid reversal is expected

modes.label: Inside fetal or exposure risk phrases
modes.description: A word within a harm phrase about pregnancy or exposure, often before its continuation.
modes.example: may cause fetal renal<< dysfunction>> leading to oligohydramnios

modes.label: Trial finding linking words
modes.description: A verb or preposition in sentences reporting trial results of risk in drug-treated patients.
modes.example: There were four suicides in drug-treated patients<< in>> the trials and none in placebo-treated patients
